author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: We need to lock down the deployment pipeline before the next retraining cycle. The hand off into model evaluation must carry a formal sign off. I am not willing to release any build that skips this step. If the evaluation does not have that documented approval attached, the deployment stays blocked. This is a hard line for the reliability team. We cannot risk shipping a model that has not been formally verified by the evaluation team. Any attempt to bypass this check will be treated as a critical incident. The sign off is mandatory for every single run, not just the major releases. We need this clarity in the contract so there is no ambiguity about who is responsible for the final gate before the model goes live.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a mandatory sign-off requirement as a 'hard line' and states that bypassing it will be treated as a critical incident, indicating a non-negotiable threshold for refusal rather than a desire for more features or a trade-off.
